sentence: Pan flipped. Pan flipped off the stove and the burner is exposed and the curtain is right above it and the curtain is moving in the draft and any second it is going to swing into the flame.

Wrong day. Wrong day. The interview was YESTERDAY at three and I am sitting here at three on the wrong day and I missed it and they are not going to reschedule and this was the only one I had this month.

He is choking. He is CHOKING. The grape, he just grabbed a grape and I was not looking and now his eyes are wide and he cannot breathe and I am behind him and arms around his middle and pulling up and counting and not getting it.

Mall. Lost him at the mall. He is four. He let go of my hand at the food court and now I am sprinting through the corridors yelling his name and security is doing a code Adam and I am picturing the worst.

The court filing window shuts at four. It is three fifty-one. The clerk's email bounced. The fax machine is making a noise I have never heard. My paralegal is on hold with the help line. Nine minutes. Nine minutes and the entire case is procedurally dead.

Best man lost the rings. Lost them. He had them this morning and now they are not in his pocket and we have searched the hotel room and the lobby and the parking lot and the ceremony starts in eighty-three minutes.

We are in the car. The wrong place. The absolute wrong place. The storm is right there, right ahead, and there is no overpass and no exit and the rain is sideways and the truck next to us is wobbling between lanes.

Closing arguments in twelve minutes and I just realized the case I was going to cite was overturned last month. Overturned. I cannot cite it. I have to restructure the entire argument. The judge has called a five-minute recess and that is not enough time.

Storm spooked her. Fireworks. She bolted from the yard and the gate was open and we have been calling and calling and the rain is heavy and the streets are slick and she does not know this neighborhood and she has no collar on.

He is on the phone the whole ride and speaking in a language I do not recognize and he keeps looking at me in the rearview mirror and we are nowhere near my destination and the route on my phone has rerouted four times.

He is detouring. He says he is detouring for gas. We just passed three gas stations. We are pulling off into a residential area and a man is standing on the corner watching us pull up and the driver is not slowing and the doors just clicked locked.

Forgot the marriage license. Forgot. The. License. We are pulling into the church and my brother just realized it is sitting on the kitchen counter in the apartment and the ceremony starts in eight minutes and you literally cannot get married without it.

I am parking. I am running. Heels in one hand, bouquet in the other, hair coming undone, mascara already on my cheek. Through the parking lot. Past the cars. The double doors are right there. They are starting the music. They are starting the music NOW.

It got quiet. Too quiet. I have been counting and it has been six minutes since the last shot and I do not know if that is good or bad and I am not moving and the kids are not moving and the radiator is clicking and the clock is ticking and outside in the hall I can hear boots.

Forgot the lyrics. Just forgot. I am at the chorus and the melody is going and my mouth is moving and only nonsense is coming out and the audience is starting to murmur and I am vamping and waiting for it to come back.

Park ranger station. Filled out the report. They are mobilizing search teams. It has been over an hour and the woods are getting dark and she is wearing a green jacket and the leaves are still green and she will be hard to see.

Heat wave. One-oh-six outside. The AC is off. The power is off and the apartments have no cross breeze and grandma is on oxygen and her concentrator runs on electricity and the battery backup is only good for an hour.

Water heater let go. The whole thing burst at the top and water is shooting straight up to the ceiling and the carpet is already soaked and I am wading toward the breaker box and there is electrical down here.
Second slide. Another section is releasing right above where we are digging and I am screaming for everyone to move and the others are not hearing me over the wind and the slope is rolling toward us.

I just saw my own stop loss get blown through. Blown straight through with no fill. The order is sitting unexecuted because there is no bid anywhere near my stop and the price is in free fall and I am about to lose three years of savings in the next four minutes.

Customs officer just said something about my name not matching the system. Not matching. He is calling a supervisor and the supervisor is taking forever and the connecting flight is in eighty minutes and customs alone takes an hour on a normal day.

Wrong patient. Wrong patient. I am pushing the heparin into the wrong central line and the patient I am dosing is going to the OR in twenty minutes and now he is anticoagulated and I have to call the surgeon and tell him and I am going to be sick.

Flight is in forty minutes. I am at the back of a customs line that is not moving. Not moving at all. There are three booths open out of twelve and the line snakes around four turns and the gate is twenty minutes walk on a good day.

Cyclist. We hit a cyclist. He is on the pavement and he is not moving and the helmet is cracked and people are getting out of their cars and someone is screaming and I am trying to dial nine-one-one and my hands are shaking so bad I keep hitting the wrong numbers.

Allergy ticket. Severe shellfish allergy on table fourteen with the linguine. The linguine has shrimp stock in it. The stock pot has been used for everything tonight. I have to start a fresh pot and the table is on a fifteen minute clock.

Forensics says the breach window started ninety days ago. NINETY days. We have no idea what is touched. We have to assume everything is touched. The CEO is on the line wanting to know what to tell the board in twenty minutes and there are no good answers.

Coyote in the yard. There is a coyote and the dog is OUT and he ran toward it and the coyote is bigger than him and I am screaming and clapping and grabbing the broom and running and they are squaring up.

Mic is dead. Microphone just died and I am singing the high note and there is no sound and the band is playing at full volume and I cannot project over them and the audience is going to wonder why I am moving my mouth silently.

The intrusion is still live. Still LIVE. We are watching them move laterally through the network in real time and the SOC is trying to cut access without tipping them off and every door we close they find another and I do not know which assets they have already touched.

Reef. We are on the reef. Hit it at six knots and the bottom is grinding and the keel is groaning and water is coming up through the floorboards and the tide is going out which means we are stuck and the boat is going to keel over.

I lock eyes with a teenage employee. Have you seen a little boy. About this tall. Curly hair. He blinks at me. I am repeating myself. Curly hair. Curly hair. He starts to answer and I am already gone, running, because he gestured vaguely toward the back of the store and I cannot wait for the rest of the sentence.

Power outage. Whole building. We are in the dark. Phones are flashlights. The man across from me is starting to panic and asking if we are going to fall and I am telling him no, the brakes are engaged, but I do not actually know if that is true.

Strangers walking with him. Strangers. I just saw him hand in hand with a man I do not know walking toward the parking lot and I am running and I am screaming and the man is looking back at me and walking faster.

He is not breathing. We dug him out and he is not breathing and he is blue around the lips and starting compressions and shouting at someone to get the ski patrol on the radio and the rescue helicopter is forty minutes out.

Turbulence severe. Severe. The plane just dropped what felt like a hundred feet and the carts hit the ceiling and the flight attendants are on the floor and the captain is yelling on the PA to stay seated and a man two rows behind me is shouting that he is having a heart attack.
Throwing up. I am about to throw up backstage and they are calling my entrance and I am bent over a bucket and the curtain just opened and the lights are on the empty stage waiting for me.

Border agent took my passport into the back room. Back room. He has not come back out for twenty minutes and the rest of the line is moving and I am sitting on a bench against the wall and other people are looking at me.
DNS is broken. DNS. Of all the things. I can't even SSH in because the bastion hostname won't resolve. The IP. What's the IP. I should have memorized the IP. Why didn't I memorize the IP.

Someone just posted a photo. A dog matching her description was hit on Madison Avenue an hour ago. The post does not say which way the dog went. I am calling the animal control number and the line is busy and I am calling the city number and the line is busy.

Smell of gasoline. Strong. Too strong. The tank must be cracked. Get everyone out. Get everyone out now. I am unbuckling the kids and the door will only open halfway. Squeeze through. The smell is getting worse. Get back. Get back from the car. How far is far enough.

Wrong graphic. The graphic that just came up has the wrong name on it. The wrong name. I have to correct it on air without making it worse and the family of the person actually mentioned might be watching and I have eight seconds to figure out the wording.

The Uber is stuck. The driver keeps saying five minutes. He has said five minutes for twenty minutes. My terminal is three exits away and traffic is not moving. I can see the planes climbing out. One of those is mine. One of those was supposed to be mine.

Kid in the deep end. Kid is panicking and kicking and going under. The mother is screaming on the side of the pool and I am the only adult in the water. Get to him. Get to him. From behind. Approach from behind so he does not climb on top of you.

Cab is pulling away and my bag was in the trunk. Cab is pulling AWAY. I am running down the street waving and yelling and he cannot hear me and the bag has my passport and my charger and the cash I changed at the airport and his license plate is mud-covered.

Hostel is locked for the night. Curfew. I do not have my keycard, my keycard was in the wallet, and I cannot remember the wifi password to call my brother. The street is empty. The street is empty and I do not know which direction to walk.

Pickpocketed. Definitely pickpocketed. There were three of them on the train and they bumped me and I felt nothing and now the wallet is gone and the phone too and I have no way to contact anyone and I am five thousand miles from home.

Smoke alarm. Smoke alarm. The hallway is full of grey. I cannot see the door at the end of it. I am crawling. Stay low. Stay low. Where is the dog. The dog. I am calling her and the smoke is going in my throat. The floor is hot. I am at the top of the stairs and the stairs look wrong, they look wrong, there is light coming up from the bottom of them.

Production is down. Down. Every second is money bleeding out and the on-call pager won't stop screaming. I'm SSHing into the box, fingers slipping, typing the wrong password twice. The CEO is in the channel asking what's happening. I don't know what's happening. Logs are flooding past faster than I can read. Something about memory, something about a deadlock. Restart the service. No, get the dump first. No, just restart, we need it up. My heart is pounding so hard I can feel it in my teeth.

Cell signal one bar. One. I am punching at the satellite messenger and the message will not send and the helicopter does not know where to go and the storm is rolling in and the visibility is dropping and the patient is fading.

Bar exam. Day two. My laptop just blue-screened. Mid-essay. I had three pages written and the screen is solid blue with a sad face on it and the proctor is walking toward me looking confused and I am about to lose my entire legal career to a Windows update.

Tour manager just quit. Quit. Mid-tour. Two hours before doors and he handed me the binder and walked out and the binder has the contracts and the float and the schedule and I have no idea what hotel we are at tomorrow.

Final exam, eighteen minutes left, three essay questions untouched. Skip the long one. Skip it. Bullet points count for partial credit. Write anything. The proctor is walking the aisles. My handwriting has gone illegible. I cannot remember the years of the Treaty. Make up a year. Just make up a year and move on.

Identity theft. The IRS just rejected my return because someone already filed using my Social Security number. Already. The deadline is in eleven hours. I am on hold with the fraud line and the hold music has been going for forty-two minutes.

Battery acid leaking from the floor scrubber. The acid is reaching the drain and the drain runs to the storm system and I am running for the absorbent pads and the supervisor is on the phone with environmental and the timer on reporting just started.

Probe hit. Probe hit something soft. He is two meters down. Digging. The snow is dense. Heavy. I am digging downhill from the strike point like they teach but the snow is cement and my back is killing me and the clock is running.

Camera went dead on a two-shot and the live audience is staring and the host is staring and I am the floor director and I have to get a working camera up in the next four seconds and the only spare is on the wrong lens.

Came home from the trip and the front door is wet. Water seeping out under it. Pushing it open and the whole entryway is flooded and the photos on the wall are warping and I can hear water still running somewhere upstairs.

I just realized the wrong file is on overleaf. I have been editing the old draft. The OLD draft. I am two days behind the actual latest version and the actual latest version is on my laptop and my laptop is at home and I am at the office and the deadline is in three hours.

S3 bucket was public. For how long. Six months. SIX MONTHS. Every backup, every export. Anybody who knew the URL could have it. We are turning off public access right now but we have to assume it is gone, gone, gone and we have to start the legal notifications.

Rain is coming down so hard I cannot see the lane lines. Wipers on max. Still cannot see. The truck ahead has hazards on. The exit sign is a blur. My mother is in surgery and I am driving forty in a sixty-five and praying.

Stuck. Stuck. The doors are not opening even at the floor. I am between the lobby and the second floor and I can see the gap and the maintenance person is on a different floor and I am claustrophobic and trying not to make a sound about it.

Suspicious package outside the federal building. They are clearing four city blocks. I work in those four city blocks. I cannot get to my car. The trains are stopped. The buses are not coming. It is dark and freezing and my phone is at six percent.

Fuel pump went out. Out. We are sitting on the shoulder of I-90 and the GPS says the nearest service station is forty-two miles back and the next show is at eight and it is already three and the tow truck is ninety minutes out.

Stroke. I think it is a stroke. Her face. One side of her face. She cannot raise her arm. The acronym. FAST. F A S T. Face, arm, speech, time. Time. Time is the one that matters and we are losing it. I have her hand and I am keeping her talking and her words are coming out wrong.

Train just slammed on the brakes. Everyone fell forward. The phone on the conductor end is going crazy and the conductor is announcing an injury on the tracks and we are not moving and the train next to us is also stopped and the tunnel is loud with alarms.

Wallet is gone. Wallet is GONE. Patting pockets. Backpack. Front pocket. Side pocket. Nothing. The metro doors are closing and I am supposed to fly out tomorrow and my passport was in the same wallet and I do not speak the language and it is past midnight.

The PA system just clicked on and an unfamiliar voice said please calmly proceed to the nearest exit. Calmly. Calmly. Nobody is calm. The chairs are going over. The double doors at the back are jammed. People are climbing over each other.

Tsunami warning. The siren just went off and they are saying inundation in twelve minutes for low-lying coastal areas and I am two blocks from the beach and the kids are at the school four blocks from the beach and the road inland is already gridlocked.

Pulse ox reads sixty-two. Sixty-two on a hundred percent. Something is wrong. Something is really wrong. Tube placement. Listen to the lungs. I hear nothing on the left. He is intubated into the right main. Pull it back. Pull it back two centimeters.

Exhibit C is missing from the binder. The judge is asking for it. The judge is asking again. I am flipping through tabs and the courtroom is silent and everyone is watching me and I cannot find the exhibit anywhere and my paralegal is texting me back that it should be there.

Voir dire. They are seating the jury. My peremptories are gone and the juror in seat seven has a brother who was prosecuted by my client's brother and the judge is asking if I want to challenge for cause and I have ninety seconds to make this call.

The dressing room attendant says she did not see anyone go in alone. The whole rack of dresses I last saw him near is a wall of fabric now and I am yanking each one aside like he might be folded behind it. He is not. He is not. My chest is so tight I am barely breathing.

Carnival. Thousands of people. I had her on my shoulders and she said she wanted to walk and I put her down and now the crush of the crowd has separated us and I cannot see over the heads and I am calling her name into the music and the music is louder than my voice.

Kill the deploy. Kill it now. The new build is OOM-killing every pod and we're cascading. I can see the graph going vertical. Rolling back. Why is the rollback hanging. Why is it hanging. Twelve thousand users on the error page right now and the number is climbing.

Earpiece keeps dropping. I am missing every cue. I cannot tell when to throw to break and I just talked over the bumper music and the audio guy is sprinting across the studio with a backup pack and the camera does not stop.

Trailer detached. Trailer detached from the truck and rolled backward into the loading bay and crushed the dock plate and there were two guys at the dock plate and now one of them is on the floor not moving and the other is screaming.

Closet. Hiding in the closet. The kids and I are in the closet and I have the phone on silent and the dispatcher is on the other end and I can hear them in the hall and they are getting closer and one of the kids whimpered.

Walk-in is warm. Walk-in is WARM. The compressor died sometime in the last hour and the protein is at fifty-two and the line is in the weeds and we need to figure out what is salvageable and what gets eighty-sixed and the temperature is still climbing.

Five minutes. He has been missing for five minutes and I am at the visitor center asking them to make an announcement and they are slow and the woman at the counter is asking me to fill out a form first and I just snapped at her.

Snow. Snow we did not expect. Eight inches in three hours and the bus is on chains and we are still 180 miles out from the next city and the show was supposed to start in two hours and we are crawling at fifteen miles an hour.

Twenty-three kids in the classroom. Lights off. Curtains drawn. We are sitting on the floor against the wall away from the door and one of the kids is sobbing and another one is laughing nervously and I just heard footsteps in the hallway and they stopped right outside.

Footsteps on the stairs. I locked the bedroom door but the bedroom door is hollow and the steps are coming up and I am whispering to nine-one-one and the dispatcher is asking me my address and I cannot remember my own address right now.

Submission portal just changed the requirements. They added a new statement we need to include and the deadline is in eighteen minutes and the statement is two pages of legalese I have to read and adapt and I have not slept in twenty-six hours.

Driver does not speak English. We are at the airport and he is taking the freight lane and I am pointing at terminal 3 on the map and he is nodding and we are pulling into the cargo area and the security guard at the gate is waving us off.

Crowded train. Crush at the doors. Someone fell on the platform side and is half in the door and the door is trying to close on him and the train is starting to inch forward and people are screaming for the conductor to hit the emergency.

V-fib. He is in v-fib. Charge to two hundred. Clear. Shock. Pulse check. Still v-fib. Charge again. Clear. Shock. The family is in the hall. Somebody close the door. Compressions, deeper, deeper, you are not getting deep enough.

Hives spreading. Spreading across the chest and up the neck. He ate a bite of something with peanut. He is wheezing. Ambulance is twenty minutes out and the second epipen is at home and we are at the restaurant.
Got it out. Got the piece out. He is gasping. He is gasping but breathing and I am sobbing and holding him and the dog is barking and my hands will not stop shaking and I think I might pass out.

Phone. Where is my phone. I need to call 911. The flames are at the curtain. I am patting my pockets and they are empty and I do not even remember where I left it. Just go. Just go. Call from outside. From the neighbor. From anywhere. Move.
Coughing fit. I cannot stop coughing. I am on camera and I am coughing into my sleeve and the producer is trying to find someone to throw to and I cannot speak and there is no break to cut to.

Ten minutes. He has been missing for ten minutes. I am cataloguing what he was wearing. Green pants. Or was it the dinosaur shirt. I cannot remember what I dressed him in this morning. How do I not know this. The security guy needs a description and I am giving him three different shirts.

Shaking. Real shaking. The bookshelf just walked off the wall. Get under the desk. Get UNDER. The pendant lamp is swinging in a circle and the windows are creaking and the dog is screaming under the bed and I am trying to remember if you stand in the doorway or if that is wrong now.

Health records. The breach included health records. HIPAA notification clock just started and we are on the phone with outside counsel and counsel is telling us we have sixty days but the records are already being traded and the news desks are picking up the story now.

Hairdresser is forty-five minutes late. The photographer is here. The mother of the bride is here. The bride is half-done with hair sticking out every direction and the first look is supposed to happen in eighteen minutes and the woman is not picking up her phone.

Sump pump is off. Storm is coming. Storm is coming and the basement is going to flood within an hour and the power is out citywide and the utility ETA is six to eight hours and the basement has all the equipment from the business in it.

Hotel after hotel saying no vacancy. Eight calls so far. We are driving into the dark with two kids in the back and no destination and the weather radio keeps saying the storm has shifted west, west toward us, and every shelter we pass has a line snaking out the door.

The chaplain just walked into the waiting room and looked at me. Just looked at me. He has not said anything yet and I know what it is going to be and I am standing up and I am not breathing and I am asking him please don't, please don't say it, please.

Twelve minutes into the code. We are at twelve minutes. Pulse check. Asystole. Twelve more minutes of this. The wife is sobbing in the hall and I can hear her through the door and I have to keep my voice steady when I run the code because the team is watching me and if I lose it they lose it.

Phone died. The map died. I do not know where the hotel is and the driver is asking and I am scrolling through dead apps and the screen is black and the airport is forty minutes behind us and we are on an interstate I have never heard of.

I forgot the name of the interviewer. I am about to walk in and I forgot her name. I had it. I had it ten minutes ago. Phone is in airplane mode for the interview. Turn it off airplane mode. Find the email. The email is loading. The email is LOADING. I am at the door.

Trail. Hiking trail. The kids were ahead of us by twenty feet and we rounded a corner and they were not there. Not on the trail, not at the lookout. We are calling their names and there is a side path we did not see and the trees are dense.

Lost the news feed. The wire is silent. I am supposed to read the top of the hour news in forty seconds and the printer has nothing and the website is loading and the deadline is closing and my heart is in my throat.

Mobile home park. We live in a mobile home park. The shelter is three blocks away and the warning just went off and we have to run and grandma cannot run and I have to carry her and the wind is already at our backs and the door is fighting me on the way out.

Pipe burst. PIPE BURST. The basement is filling. I can hear it from upstairs and the water is already at the second step and I cannot find the shut-off valve and I do not know if it is in the basement or in the front yard.

The shuttle from long-term parking is sitting at the wrong terminal. Driver, please, this is the wrong terminal. I have a flight. He shrugs. I am opening the door at a red light and running across four lanes of dropoff traffic. A horn blares. I do not look. The departures sign keeps blinking.

Sump pump failed. Power is out and the backup battery is dead and the rain has not stopped and the basement is up to my knees and rising and the furnace is going to be underwater in five minutes and there is nothing I can do.

Replication lag is six hours and climbing. Six hours. The read replicas are serving stale data and we just shipped an order confirmation to a customer for a product we already sold out of. How many. How many customers got the wrong page. I need to pull a query and I need to pull it now.

Prompter died. Whole prompter went dark and I am improvising and the script was twelve paragraphs of detailed quote attribution and now I am trying to remember which side said what and the seconds are ticking and the executive producer is pacing behind the cameras.

Done. Hit submit. Hit submit and the portal threw an error and said try again later and now I have to refresh and it is showing as not received and I cannot tell if the previous attempt actually went through and if I submit again it might double-submit and disqualify me.

I had it at dinner. I had it at the restaurant. Running back. Two blocks back. Three blocks. The restaurant is closed. The metal gate is pulled down. I am banging on it and no one is answering and the lights are off.

We are live in three. Three. The chyron is wrong, the prompter just froze, the producer is talking in my earpiece and I cannot hear what she is saying and the floor manager is counting down with his fingers and I am the only person who is supposed to be talking in fifteen seconds.

Conference abstract closes at noon UTC. It is eleven fifty-eight. I am still fixing the title because autocorrect mangled a word and now the field will not accept my edit. The character counter is red. Cut a word. Cut another word. The page has no time to wait for me to be eloquent.

Train platform. He took two steps away to look at a poster and the train pulled in and the doors opened and people got on and the doors closed and the train pulled away and he was on it. He was on it. He was on the train and I was not.

Generator failed. Building lost power and the generator did not kick on and we are on battery and we have maybe two minutes of battery and the morning show is in the middle of a sponsor read and I cannot tell them yet because that would be worse.

Cart machine just spat out a blank. I queued the spot and the spot played silent. Twenty seconds of silence on a national feed. I have to fill, I have to fill, I am riffing about the weather and my voice is shaking.

Every exit. Watch every exit. I am at the front of the store telling the manager to lock the doors and she is asking me to calm down. I cannot calm down. He is four. He is four. I am going to find him in the next ninety seconds or I am going to come apart in front of all these strangers.

Water is already in the street. Up to the curb. Faster than they said it would be. The rain hasn't even started yet and I am throwing photo albums into a trash bag and the kids are crying because they want their stuffed animals and I cannot find the cat.

Engineer just emailed a customer list to her personal Gmail by accident. Sent. Cannot recall. The list has fifty thousand records and the engineer is freaking out and the CISO is on the phone and we need to know in the next four minutes whether to invoke the breach disclosure clock.

Buried. I think I am buried. Cannot tell which way is up. Mouth full of snow. Spitting. Trying to clear an air pocket with my hand. The arm is pinned. The other arm. Use the other arm. Pushing the snow away from my face.
Cord prolapse. I can feel the cord in my hand. Patient is in Trendelenburg, I am holding the head off the cord, do not let me lift up, do not let me move, we are going to the OR like this. Right now.

Five minutes left and I have not even looked at section three. Five minutes. Flipping pages. Reading nothing. Just bubbling. C, C, B, C, A, anything, please, just put something down for every question.

Driver is going the wrong way. The wrong way. I see the highway he should have taken on the right and we are heading left and the rate is climbing and he is not responding when I tap his shoulder and the doors are locked.

TSA pulled my bag. They are unpacking it on the table and the line is held up and the boarding gate is closing in twelve minutes and I cannot tell what they are looking at and they keep asking me to wait.

Ice broke. Somebody just broke through the ice on the pond and the dog ran out to them and now the dog is in the water too and they are clawing at the edge of the hole and the ice keeps breaking and I cannot get close because it will break under me too.

Visa was supposed to be in the email. Is not. The hotel printout I have is the wrong year. Customs officer is asking for proof of onward travel and I cannot find the confirmation and my phone is at three percent.

Emergency descent. Steep. We are dropping fast and my stomach is in my throat and the oxygen mask is fogged and the cabin altitude warning is sounding and a flight attendant just lost her footing and went down hard.

Pressure is bottoming out and the second pressor is not working and the lactate is sixteen and the kidneys are going and I have an attending on the phone telling me to keep going and I do not know what else to try and the patient is dying right in front of me.

Twenty minutes left. Twenty. I haven't even started the essay question and I just realized I misread the prompt for the first section. Did I answer the wrong question entirely. Flipping back. Yes. Yes I did. My stomach is in my throat and I can hear the proctor's footsteps and someone two rows over just turned in their paper.

Flight in two hours and the car has not moved in fifteen minutes. The driver is napping. NAPPING. I tapped him and he is groggy and the meter is running and I just realized he is not even logged into the app, this is not even my ride, I got in the wrong car.

I cannot find the cat. I cannot find the cat anywhere. Under the bed, in the closet, behind the dryer. The evacuation order said now. I am running out of time. The car is loaded. The cat is somewhere in the house and the sky is full of smoke.
Came home and the door was open. Open. The lock is broken and the door is just slightly ajar and I do not know if they are still inside and I am standing on the porch and I should not go in.

My daughter was in the back seat. She is crying. That is good. Crying is good. Crying means breathing. I am unbuckling and trying to get to her and my own door is jammed. Climb over the console. Climb. The car seat looks fine. She looks fine. Please be fine please be fine please be fine.

VIP. VIP on table eleven. Critic. Critic in the dining room. The expo is whispering it down the line and now every hand is shaking and the chef de cuisine is staring at the pass and the plate I just sent has a thumb print on the rim.

Pulled him out. He is blue. He is blue around the lips. Not breathing. Tilt the head. Two breaths. Watch the chest. The chest is not rising. Try again. The water is coming out of his mouth. Roll him. Roll him on his side now.

Three down. Three down at the corner of the building. I am running with the kit and the rounds are still coming in over my head and the corpsman is yelling for cover and the first guy is bleeding from the femoral and I have ten seconds before he is gone.

Gas line. I can smell gas. The shaking stopped and now I smell gas and I have to turn off the main but the main is in the side yard and the side yard is full of fallen brick and I do not have shoes on and the kids are still crying upstairs.

Baby is crying in the back. The car seat is intact and the baby is crying which is good but I cannot turn around because my neck. My neck. I cannot turn my neck. And the other driver is at my window screaming at me.

Engine just failed. Right engine. The plane is yawing and the captain is on the rudder and the warning horn is going and the passengers are looking at the wing and the wing has a smoke trail behind it.
Sleeve. My sleeve is on fire. The sleeve of my sweater. Stop drop and roll, stop drop and roll, I am on the kitchen floor rolling and screaming and my husband is running toward me with a blanket.

Roof leak became a roof breach. Water and chunks of insulation pouring down on the inventory and the electrical panel is right under it and the sparks are starting and I am running for the breaker and someone is yelling to get out.

Power is out. Water is out. The cell network is jammed. I cannot get a call out and I cannot get a text out and my mother is in a nursing home on the third floor of a building I do not know if is still standing and I am five hours away.

Sound check. We are at sound check and the monitor system is completely silent. Silent. They have been trying for two hours and the show is in forty minutes and the band cannot hear themselves and the engineer is sweating and pulling cables.

Caterer just called. Caterer just called and said they double-booked and they cannot do our wedding tonight. Tonight. Server farm. Power went down and the diesel did not start. Did not start. The UPS is giving us seven minutes and the team is on the phone screaming at the facilities guy and the racks are running on battery and the lights are red.

The basement furnace exploded. I felt it through the floor. The whole house jumped. I am pulling the kids off the couch and we are running for the front door and I do not even have shoes on. Outside. Outside. Get to the street. Get away from the windows. The windows could go any second.
Pool deck. He was at the pool deck. Just three feet ahead. I turned to grab the towel and he is not there and the pool is right there and I am scanning the water first before anything else.

Decel. Long decel. Down to sixty for over a minute. Repositioning. Oxygen on. Still down. Internal monitor not picking up. I cannot tell if this is real. I cannot tell if I am chasing a bad signal. The OB is not answering the page and I am the senior nurse on the floor.

Final boarding call for flight 1142 to Frankfurt. That is me. That is me. I am still at customs. The agent is reading my landing card line by line. Sir. Sir. My plane. He does not look up. There is no version of this where I do not miss the connection. My whole onward itinerary is collapsing.

Amniotic fluid embolism. She just dropped. Pressure tanked. Sat tanked. Crashing. Crashing right now. The husband is screaming. The crash cart is being pushed across the room and I am hanging blood and I cannot remember her name.

He was right next to me. Right next to me one second and now he is gone. Spinning. Spinning in every direction at the playground and yelling his name and the other parents are turning to look and the gate is open and the street is right there.

Kids are in the next room. The kids. The door is locked but they are in another room and I have to get to them and I cannot make a sound and I am crawling on the floor and the floorboards creak no matter where I step.

Submission portal closes in eleven minutes. Eleven. I am converting the file to PDF and the formatting just broke and the figures are not embedding and the upload is going to need three more files I do not have ready yet.

Tax filing deadline. Eleven fifty-three at night. The software wants a verification code that should have come three minutes ago. Check spam. Check trash. Resend. Resend. Resend. My speech. My speech is on a phone that is at four percent battery and the cable does not fit any of the chargers in this building and the toasts start in nineteen minutes and I cannot remember a single line of what I wrote.

Beacon. Switching the beacon to search. Skinning back uphill. Sweep pattern, sweep pattern. The signal is faint. Closer. Closer. The arrow is pointing down. He is under here. Get the probe out. Get the shovel.

Smell of gas. Strong. After the crash the smell of gas is everywhere and I am dragging my passenger out by the shoulders and the door is half-open and the engine is ticking and there are sparks somewhere I cannot see.

Pull the airbag. PULL THE AIRBAG. Where is the handle. The handle on the strap. Got it. Pulling. The bag inflated. I am being swept and the bag is keeping me up and the snow is in my mouth and I cannot breathe through the powder.

1099 missing. Cannot find the 1099 from the brokerage and the broker website is down for maintenance and customer service is closed and the return cannot be filed without that number and the rest of the form is already done.

She is unresponsive. UNRESPONSIVE. The epi went in and she still is not responding and I am checking the pulse and the pulse is there but barely and I do not know if it is the reaction or the epi or what is happening and the operator is asking me questions I cannot answer.

Boarding now. I am running with my carry-on flapping behind me and the moving walkway is broken and people are blocking the right side and I am yelling excuse me and the gate is at C47 and I am at C12.

Wait. Wait. The date on the cover is wrong. This is last year's exam. This is the wrong exam. Am I in the wrong room. Looking around. Everyone else has the same booklet. So this IS the right one and they just printed the wrong year. Don't think about it don't think about it just start writing.

Chest wound. Sucking chest wound. Air going in and out of the hole and I am tearing the seal package open and slapping it on and the patient is panicking and I cannot get him to lie still and the medevac is twelve minutes out.

Daycare just called. Daycare just called and said he choked on something and they are doing the Heimlich and he is breathing now but they want me to come and the ambulance is also coming and I am running for my keys.

Caller is going off the rails. He just said a slur on air and the dump button is jammed and the seven-second delay is gone and the GM is going to fire me and the producer is making throat-cut signs and I am scrambling to cut to commercial.
Hospital parking garage is full. FULL. I am circling level after level and there is nowhere and I just abandoned the car on the curb by the emergency room entrance and I do not care if they tow it.

Lockdown alarm. This is not a drill. The principal said this is not a drill on the intercom. We are pulling kids in off the playground and locking the door and pushing the bookshelf in front of it and the kids are crying and I am telling them to be quiet and I cannot stop my hands from shaking.

Discovered last year's return was wrong. The CPA put the wrong figure in the depreciation schedule and it cascaded. I need to amend and pay back and the statute on the audit window closes today and if I do not file the amendment today they could come after the full amount plus penalties.

Schools went into lockdown. Lockdown. Not lockout, lockdown. My kids are in there and the news is showing helicopter footage and the helicopter is over the elementary school where my daughter is and I am driving and the road to the school is blocked and I do not know what to do.
The sky is orange. The sky is ORANGE. At noon. Ash is falling like snow on the porch and the wind is hot and I can see the glow at the ridge and the alert just upgraded from warning to evacuate.

My phone has not stopped ringing since the bell. Clients. Every client. Each one wants to know what to do and I do not know what to do and I cannot tell them I do not know because I am supposed to be the one with the answers and the screens are red across every sector.

The storm is supposed to make landfall in nine hours and the gas station is out of gas. Both gas stations in town are out. The line at the third one is around the block and the tanker hasn't shown up and we still have to load the dog and grandma and the cat and we have not boarded a single window.

Wifi is out. Wifi is out at home and the interview is in three minutes and the hotspot is being throttled and the video call quality is going to make me look like a smear and there is no time to drive somewhere with wifi and they are going to log on and see a frozen face.

School nurse just called. Anaphylaxis. She gave the epipen and he is breathing easier and the ambulance is coming and the school is asking me which hospital to go to and I have to call my husband and I cannot remember our pediatrician's phone number.
Hit something. Hit something hard. The bow is taking on water and we are going down by the bow and I am running for the life raft and the painter is tangled and I cannot get the raft over the rail.

Embassy is closed for the holiday. The holiday is three days. My flight is in two days. I am at the consulate gate looking at a printed sign in a language I cannot read and the only number listed goes to a recording.

Forty-five minutes from the hospital. Forty-five. The text said come now. Come now. What does come now mean. Is he. Is he still. I cannot ask. I cannot type with these hands. The exit is in two miles. Move. Move.

Heart attack. Man across from me just clutched his chest and went sideways and I am calling for help and pressing the emergency strip and the train is decelerating and we are between stations and people are pulling out their phones with no signal.

I cannot find my partner. The party was four of us and three are accounted for and the fourth is gone and his beacon is not coming through, not coming through, and the battery indicator on my unit just dropped to red.

Lost a bus. A whole bus. The B bus with the support crew is not at the venue and they were supposed to be in two hours ago and nobody is picking up phones and the trailer with the rigging is with them.

Forgot the medications. All of them. Dad's blood pressure, Mom's insulin, my anxiety meds. Lost the field reporter. Lost his signal. He was about to deliver the lead and the satellite truck is showing no feed and the director is in my ear telling me to fill and I have no notes on the story and the camera is on me.

Office on the twenty-second floor. Twenty-two flights of stairs. People stopping to catch their breath and the line backing up and the smoke alarm is going and we cannot tell if there is real smoke or if it is just the alarm and someone behind me is having an asthma attack.

Hold the door. Hold the door, hold the door, I do not care if your hands hurt, HOLD IT. The pull cord is missing. Why is the pull cord missing. Why does this classroom not have a pull cord. The handle is turning. The handle is turning.

Allergic reaction. The EpiPen. I cannot find the EpiPen. Her face is swelling. Her lips are swelling. I am tearing through the bag. Where did I put it. I always put it in the side pocket. It is not in the side pocket. The dispatcher is talking. I am not listening. Find it find it find it.

Phone call came through to the receptionist. She is shaking. She wrote down what they said. The note is going to the police now and we are being moved across the street and the SWAT vehicle just rolled up.

The agent at the desk is shaking her head. The flight is closed. I can see it through the window. The jet bridge is still attached. Please. Please call them. There is one seat. I know there is one seat. My voice is too loud. People are looking. I do not care. I cannot be here tomorrow.

Mouth-to-mouth on the side of the pool. Compressions. Where is the ambulance. The grandfather is gray and not breathing and I learned this in CPR class six years ago and I cannot remember if it is fifteen and two or thirty and two.

Hospital elevator. I am supposed to bring this code cart upstairs in the next ninety seconds and the elevator just stalled between four and five and the page is going off on my hip and I am stuck and they are coding upstairs without the cart.

Got the kids in the car and forgot the laptop. The laptop has every photo, every tax record, every business file. Should I go back. The fire is over the next hill. Should I go back. The kids are screaming for me not to go back.

I left the cheat sheet in the bathroom. I left it on the counter. The proctor went into the bathroom after me. Did they see it. Did they SEE IT. I am about to be expelled and I cannot focus on a single problem because I am waiting for the tap on the shoulder.

I skipped a page. I skipped a page of dialogue. The other actor is staring at me waiting for a line I already said and now nothing makes sense and the audience knows something is wrong and the prompter is offstage hissing something I cannot hear.

Cell phone has no service. None. I am punching the alarm button and shouting and pulling out a credit card to try to wedge the doors and the cards bend but the doors do not budge and the air feels hotter every minute.

I think those guys are following me. I crossed the street twice and they crossed too. Walk faster. Walk faster but do not look back. The hotel is six blocks. They are gaining. Why are they gaining. I do not even have anything left for them to take.

Suspicious package under the seat. The conductor's announcement said evacuate at next station and the next station is nine minutes away and I am staring at the bag and trying not to look at it and the train is going slower than usual.

The kitchen. Oil fire. I left the pan. I left the pan on. The flames are up the cabinets. I am screaming for everyone to get out. Get out. Get out. The smoke detector is shrieking. I am throwing a lid at the pan and missing. Where is the baking soda. Where is the baking soda. Just go. Just go. Leave it.

Conference center. Five thousand attendees. Nobody knows the floor plan. The exit signs only point one way and there is already a crush at that door. I am turning the other way to find a different exit and three people grab my arm and tell me no, that way is closed.

Other car is in the ditch. The driver is slumped over the wheel. I am running across the lanes and the windshield is spider-webbed and there is steam coming up and I am pulling at the door handle and the door will not open and I can see he is not moving.

Compliance just emailed. They want positions flat by close. Every position. I have eighty open trades across forty-two symbols and the market is broken and the bid-ask spreads are wider than the daily range and I have four hours to unwind everything without blowing the book up further.

Elevator stopped. Lights flickered. Now we are between floors and the emergency button is not doing anything. I am pressing it and pressing it and there is no voice on the other end and the woman next to me is starting to hyperventilate.

Hot water heater connection split. Boiling water hitting the floor. Steam everywhere. The pets are upstairs and I have to get to the breaker first and then the valve and then the pets and the steam is making it hard to see.

Two of them. There are two of them. I can hear two different voices downstairs and they are not whispering, they are talking like they think the house is empty and I am upstairs and the only way down is past them.

We are on the eighth floor. The eighth floor and the building is swaying. Swaying like a slow tree. I can see the building across the street swaying the other way and they are about to swing into each other and the windows here are starting to pop.

The address. What is my address. I am standing in my own house and I am blanking on the number. Two something. Two two something. The 911 operator is patient. I am not. There is a man on the floor and I do not know my own house number. The street. I know the street. I am yelling the street name.

Bird is six minutes. Six minutes. Patient is in shock, BP barely palpable, IV running wide open with fluids and the fluids are not catching up to the bleed and we cannot stop all of it and the helicopter is six minutes and he might not have six minutes.

There is a head bobbing past the buoy. Going under. Going under again. I am yelling for the lifeguard and the lifeguard is already running and I am pulling off my shirt because I can swim and the head went under a third time and did not come back up.
Heel snapped on the entrance. The whole heel just snapped off and I am limping with one shoe four inches taller than the other and the next move is a downstage cross and the spotlight is on me.

The other driver is getting out of his car and walking toward me and he is yelling. I do not know what happened. I think the light was green. I think it was green. He is in my face. My hands are up. I just need to call someone. Just let me call someone. My phone is somewhere on the road.

On a plane. He is on a plane and just ate something with shellfish and the flight attendants are paging for a doctor and the doctor is back in row 32 and they are trying to find the medical kit and we are over the ocean an hour from any airport.

Security pulls up the camera. There. There she is. Aisle nine, eleven minutes ago, holding hands with someone. Who is that. I cannot see the face. I cannot see her face. The guard is rewinding and I want him to go faster. Faster. Just play it forward. Just show me where she is right now.

Water in the cabin. Water in the CABIN. The hull is breached. The bilge pump is running but losing and the swim ladder is gone and the radio is just static and I am scanning the horizon for any other boat.

Her face is swelling. Tongue thickening. She is trying to ask me something and I cannot understand and her lips are turning purple and I am calling for help and the lifeguard is not answering and the front desk is empty.

My passport. Where is my passport. I had it at the kiosk. It is not in my back pocket. It is not in my jacket. It is not in the front pouch of the bag. Oh god. The line behind me is six people deep and they all see it on my face. I am going to be the person who held everyone up.

Saucier just cut himself. Bad. Blood everywhere on the station. I am pulling him off the line and tying off the bleed and the printer is still spitting tickets and pasta is on the fire and the sauce is about to break.

String broke mid-concerto. The G string. Snapped. I am playing on three strings and the orchestra is fifty bars from the end and I have to make it without that string and the rest of the section is whispering and the conductor noticed.

Wife is calling. Wife is calling and she just saw the news and she is asking if we lost the down payment for the house and I do not have time to answer and the answer is yes and I have to keep working because if I stop right now we lose even more.

Hail. Golf-ball hail. The size of fists, actually, fists. The skylight just shattered and the glass is everywhere and the wind is coming in and we are getting away from the windows and toward the interior bathroom but there is glass on the floor and I do not have shoes on.

Interview started fourteen minutes ago. Fourteen minutes ago. My alarm did not go off. My alarm DID NOT GO OFF. I am pulling on slacks and my shirt at the same time and the laptop is booting and the link is buried in my email and I am searching frantically and they are going to think I ghosted them.

Hours of searching. Hours. Posting on every neighborhood group. Flyers. Driving every street. Calling her name out the window. The light is fading and the temperature is dropping and she has never been outside alone overnight and she has anxiety.

Cabin pressure. Oxygen masks dropped. The masks dropped over every seat and the captain is announcing rapid descent and my ears are popping and the baby in the row ahead is screaming and the mother cannot get her mask on first because the baby is screaming.

Departure board updated. Gate change. From B12 to D44. That is a forty minute walk in a normal airport. Boarding in fourteen minutes. I am already running before my brain has caught up to the new letter. People are pulling their kids out of my way. I have never moved this fast in dress shoes.

Sheriff is in the driveway. The sheriff. He just pounded on the door and said leave now, leave now, the fire turned and is coming this way and we have ten minutes maybe and I am throwing the photo albums and the kids and the dog into the car.

Witness just contradicted herself on the stand. The whole defense theory is built on her timeline. The opposing counsel is grinning. The jury is whispering. I have to redirect in three minutes and I have not thought of how to fix this and my client is staring at me from the defendant's table.

School just called. School just called and said something about a fall and they are calling an ambulance and they could not tell me how bad it is and I am in the car already and the seatbelt is not buckled and I do not care and I am running yellows and I will run reds if I have to.

Salamander broke. The salamander broke and I have eight steaks to finish and the broilers are full and I am improvising with a torch and the torch is running out of butane and the table is waiting and the GM is in the kitchen which never happens at this hour.

Laptop battery just died mid-interview. I left the charger at home. The hotspot is at four percent. I am running to the front desk to ask if they have a charger and the interviewer is on the other end of the call and the call dropped and I cannot rejoin without the laptop.

We are out. We are on the lawn. I am counting heads. One. Two. Three. Where is four. Where is four. He was right behind me. I am running back toward the door and the firefighter is grabbing me by the shoulders and saying ma'am ma'am and I am not stopping. He is in there.

Got him in the car. Got him in the car and he was limping and there is blood on the back seat and I do not know where the blood is coming from and the emergency vet is closed and the second-nearest one is forty minutes away.

Costume malfunction. The zipper. The zipper just came down at the back of the dress mid-song and I cannot reach it and the next move is a full turn and the audience is going to see and the choreographer is in the front row.

Lost a passenger. Medical. Heart attack in row 22. The flight attendants are doing compressions in the aisle and the AED is hooked up and the captain is diverting to the nearest field and we are still forty minutes out.

The window. The bedroom window. I cannot get it open. The frame has been painted shut for a decade. I am hitting the latch with the heel of my shoe. The smoke is pushing into the room from under the door. I can see it. I can see it like a slow grey snake. The shoe is not working. Get the chair. Get the chair.

Audit letter just arrived. They want documentation for the last three years and they want it in thirty days and the records are in a storage unit and the storage unit changed owners and the new owners say the unit was cleared out six months ago.

Postpartum hemorrhage. She is bleeding too much. Pitocin in. Methergine in. Hemabate. The fundus is boggy. Massage. Massage harder. Get the balloon. Get blood. Get four units of blood up here in the next ten minutes.

She fell. She fell off the ladder. Her leg is bent the wrong way. She is screaming. I cannot move her. I am not supposed to move her. The dispatcher is telling me to keep her still and I am holding her down because she is trying to sit up and the bone is sticking through the skin and I am not going to throw up I am not going to throw up.

Five minutes to the end of the trading session and the order is hung. The confirmation will not come through. The market is moving against me by the second. Cancel. Resubmit. The platform is asking me to log in again. I am going to be down six figures by the time this clears.

Circuit breaker tripped at the seven percent mark. Trading halted for fifteen minutes. Fifteen minutes of staring at the screen with my heart hammering and the futures still falling and knowing that when it reopens it is going to be worse.

Mall. We are at the mall and people are running from the food court and there is screaming and I grabbed my daughter and we ducked into a store and the manager is pulling down the metal gate and I do not know what is happening but the running is enough, the running is enough to know.
Sky just turned black at three in the afternoon. Streetlights came on. The wind died completely. Birds are silent. This is the calm before. This is the calm before. Get inside. Get inside NOW.

Dead air. Dead air just hit. The board went dark and the song stopped halfway through and the engineer is sprinting from the back and I am alone in the studio and the mic is hot and I have to say something and I cannot think of anything to say.

She is seizing. On the kitchen floor. She is seizing. I am on hands and knees holding her head off the tile. The phone is on speaker. The voice is telling me not to put anything in her mouth. I am crying and saying I know I know I know. How long has this been. I have lost track.

Stoplight at the intersection is out. Out and the four-way is not being respected and cars are flying through and I am at the corner about to cross and someone just got hit and there is shouting and people are running.

The toy section. He has to be in the toy section. He is not in the toy section. I am pushing carts out of my way. A woman asks if I am okay. I cannot answer. My mouth is open and nothing comes out. I am thinking about the parking lot. The doors of this store open straight onto a parking lot.

I just realized the cookies had walnuts. Walnuts. He just ate two. He is allergic to walnuts. He is asking me why his mouth feels weird and I am running for the kitchen drawer where the epi is supposed to be and it is not there.

Riptide. Riptide has him and he is going out, not in. He is screaming and people on the beach are pointing and a man is running into the surf with a boogie board and I do not know if anybody actually called nine-one-one yet.

Train just stopped between stations. Lights flickered off, then dim emergency only. The conductor said something but the speakers are blown and nobody could understand it. The man next to me is breathing too fast and the woman across is asking out loud what is happening.

Horses. We have horses and the trailer is on the other side of the property and the wind shifted and the smoke is so thick I cannot see them in the pasture and the gate is open and the road out is one lane and already gridlocked.

Construction. There is construction on the highway and I am sitting in stopped traffic and I can see the hospital tower in the distance and I cannot get to it and my sister is calling again, calling again, and I cannot pick up because I cannot hear what she is going to say.

Source code repo is public. PUBLIC. Some intern pushed the org's main monorepo to their personal GitHub. It has been mirrored already. Several mirrors. We are filing takedowns and the takedowns will take days and by then the credentials in the repo will all be exploited.

Sliding glass door. They came through the sliding glass door and broke the lock and I can see footprints in the carpet leading toward the office and the office has the safe and the safe is bolted but the safe is not fireproof and I do not even know what is in the safe.

Fire on the line. The grease in the fryer caught and the flames are at the hood and the suppression system has not triggered and the fire extinguisher is at the back of the kitchen and the diners can see into the kitchen through the pass.

Forklift tipped. The forklift tipped on the loading dock and the operator went out the side and the cage was not down and the forks are pinning him to the pavement and we are running and trying to lift it and it is too heavy.

The transfer in Doha is forty-five minutes and I have already burned thirty of it in the immigration queue. The next gate is in a different terminal. There is a train. I do not know which train. I am scanning the signage and the Arabic is gorgeous and useless to me right now. Run. Just run.

She is desatting. Seventy. Sixty-eight. Bag her, bag her. The vent disconnected. The vent disconnected at the wye and nobody saw it and the saturation is dropping and the alarm is going and I am reaching for the ambu bag and my gloves are not on yet.

Wrong building. I am in the wrong building. They have three buildings on the campus and I went to the one with the same name on it and the interview is in another one twelve minutes walk away and I am supposed to be sitting down right now.

Roof. The roof is the only way out. The fire escape is engulfed. I am at the top of the apartment building in my socks and a tee shirt and the firefighters are below me with a ladder that does not look long enough. They are yelling something. I cannot hear over the sirens. They want me to jump. They want me to jump.

Trees are already coming down two streets over. We can hear them. Each one is a crack and a long groan and then the impact. The dog is hiding under the bed. I cannot get him out and the SUV is loaded and we need to leave now, NOW.

Black ice. The car is sliding sideways and the guardrail is coming and we are going to roll. We are going to ROLL. Bracing. Bracing. The world is turning over and over and I do not know how to stop my head from hitting the window.

Tourniquet on. Tourniquet ON. Cranking. Cranking until the windlass locks. The leg is white below the knee. The bleeding stopped. Next. Move to the next patient. Where is the next patient. Behind the wall. Drag him. Drag him.

School called. They put the kids in the hallway. They put the kids in the hallway and the funnel is half a mile from the school and I am twenty minutes away and I cannot do anything. I cannot do anything. I am driving and crying and I do not even know which direction the school is.
